title: Grace is justly withheld from the guilty
source_text: XXI. Quibus addit, gratiam iis quibus negatur juste a Deo negari, propterea quod culpa sua indignos se ea reddiderunt, unde est quod ejus carentia non possit excusare eorum impotentiam ad benefaciendum. Secus vero futurum si Deus creaturam omni peccato carentem destitueret auxiliis necessariis ad bene agendum: tum enim nullam fore in creatura culpam, quoniam in eo sequeretur Dei institutionem, nec dici posset ab ea recessisse.
pass_a_gloss: XXI. To which he adds, that grace to those to whom it is denied is justly denied by God, because by their fault they have rendered themselves unworthy of it, whence it is that the lack of it cannot excuse their inability for doing good. But otherwise it would be if God should leave a creature lacking all sin destitute of the helps necessary for acting well: for then there would be no fault in the creature, since in that it would follow the institution of God, nor could it be said to have departed from it.
pass_b_english: Thesis XXI. He adds that when God withholds grace from people he withholds it justly, because by their own fault they have made themselves unworthy of it. So its absence cannot excuse their inability to do good.

It would be different, he says, if God deprived a creature free of all sin of the aids it needs to act rightly. Then the creature would bear no blame, since in that respect it would simply be following the order God had set, and could not be said to have departed from it.

lemmas.latin: culpa sua indignos se ea reddiderunt
lemmas.gloss: by their fault they have rendered themselves unworthy of it
it would follow the institution of God

choices.why: The divine auxilium of the de auxiliis debates; 'help' in the literal pass, 'aid' or 'help' in the reading.

bible_refs: Cornelius Jansenius, Augustinus (Louvain, 1640), tome 3, De gratia Christi Salvatoris.
